Night Market brings independent kitchens into one shared courtyard. Guests can taste small dishes, meet the makers and stay for live acoustic sets.
The proposed event welcomes local residents, nearby workers and visitors looking for an informal evening. Clear menus help groups with different preferences choose together.
Sponsors help fund the shared seating, music and waste collection. Their presence is built around useful services that improve the experience for guests.
A hot griddle anchors the savoury offering. Small portions keep the queue moving and give visitors room to try another kitchen later.
A seasonal vegetable counter adds freshness to the menu. Clearly displayed ingredients make it easier for guests to ask informed questions before ordering.
A bakery stall serves small desserts and warm drinks through the evening. Its later service window gives guests a reason to stay after dinner.
Begin with a small savoury dish and a drink. Place tasting portions near the front of the menu so first-time visitors can choose quickly.
Invite guests to discover another kitchen across the courtyard. A printed tasting card helps them remember what they tried and where it came from.
Finish with dessert near the music area. Shared seating encourages visitors to linger while keeping the space in front of each counter clear.
Welcome the first guests while the courtyard is still light. Give each kitchen time to settle into service before the first scheduled performance.
Bring the main music set into the centre of the evening. Keep sound levels appropriate for ordering and conversation near the food counters.
Announce final food orders before the music ends. Leave a clear interval for guests to finish eating and for vendors to close their stations.
Place the welcome point where visitors enter naturally. Show the kitchen locations and facilities before guests join a queue or settle at a table.
Keep the middle of the courtyard open for communal seating. The arrangement should let groups see the music while maintaining a clear circulation route.
Give vendors access to their service areas from the perimeter. Confirm power and waste arrangements before allocating the final pitches to participating kitchens.
Support the shared seating and drinking-water station. Recognition appears where the service is used, with a short acknowledgement in the printed event guide.
Fund the performance programme and the sound crew. Include a host acknowledgement and a credit beside the evening schedule at the welcome point.
Support the wider event infrastructure and vendor preparation. Agree a clear package of recognition across the event guide and pre-event communications.
The chart uses an illustrative allocation to show how the event proposal can communicate its priorities. Final amounts depend on the venue and supplier quotes.
Seating, access and basic services receive funding before optional decoration. These shared facilities support every kitchen and every visitor during the evening.
Confirm each supplier's scope before committing the spend. Keep a reserve for changes that become clear during the final site walk.
Ask participating kitchens to share the event with their regular guests. Give every vendor the same opening hours, address and booking information.
Use a small number of clearly placed posters near the venue. Put the date and location above supporting details so passers-by can read them quickly.
Publish the kitchen lineup and practical arrival information during the final week. Update the same channels if weather changes the planned programme.
Give every vendor a clear plan
Send each kitchen its pitch, setup window and facilities list. Confirm the person responsible for answering questions during loading and installation.
Keep a named coordinator available throughout the event. Share how vendors should report supply problems or a queue that begins to obstruct movement.
Agree the collection point for waste and the order of vehicle access. Record any issues while the team is together so the next event improves.
Reserve a place at the table
Invite sponsors to choose the service they want to support. Agree the recognition, contribution and delivery responsibilities before artwork enters production.
Confirm the kitchen lineup and performance schedule together. Check that each part of the evening has the facilities and staffing it requires.
Complete the final site walk with vendors and the venue team. Share one current event plan so everyone works from the same information.
